_header: Generated by driving the real Rust at 9023b46d with
FROZEN: nothing regenerates this. A diff is a defect in the port.
state_after records the context fields these commands can move,
so a set that writes the wrong field is visible.

tools.name: the furnished surface, with every warning kind
tools.note: Three warning kinds: an unknown tool in enabled_tools, an undefined subagent in enabled_subagents, and a subagent referencing a tool that does not exist.

tools.name: an empty config still lists every registered tool
tools.note: The roster is the registry's, not the config's — only `main` changes.

config_check.name: a config with a missing api key env var
config_check.note: `SHORE_FIXTURE_KEY_SET` is set and `SHORE_FIXTURE_KEY_MISSING` is not, so exactly one model warns.

warnings: API key env var $SHORE_FIXTURE_KEY_MISSING not set (needed by model chat.anthropic.secondary)

config_check.name: no models at all
config_check.note: The no-models warning fires and the no-default-model warning does not — it is gated on the catalog being non-empty.

warnings: No chat models configured. Add a [providers.*] entry and set [defaults].model to a provider:model_id.

config_check.name: an api key env var that is set but empty
config_check.note: `std::env::var` gives `Ok("")`, so a blank value counts as set and the only warning is the missing default model.

warnings: No default model set. First chat model will be used.

config_check.name: a default model that is not in the catalog

warnings: Default model "nonexistent" not found in catalog
API key env var $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set (needed by model chat.anthropic.primary)

config_check.name: models but no default set
config_check.note: `valid` is false: this is a warning, not info.

warnings: No default model set. First chat model will be used.
API key env var $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set (needed by model chat.anthropic.primary)

config_read.name: the whole config and the whole default baseline
config_read.note: The entire serde shape of AppConfig, twice. This is what the TypeScript serializer has to reproduce field for field.

config_read.name: one section by key
config_read.note: `defaults` is that section of the built-in defaults, not the whole baseline.

config_read.name: a map-valued section
config_read.note: The default for `subagents` is an empty map, not null.

config_read.name: a non-string key is no key at all
config_read.note: `as_str` is `None`, so this is the whole-config read.

config_read.name: a value without a key is still a read

config_set.name: defaults.model sets the session's active model
config_set.note: `active_resolved_model` is dropped so the next command re-resolves against the new name.

config_set.name: a model change drops the pre-resolved selection
config_set.note: `active_resolved_model` was populated and is null afterwards: the pre-resolved value no longer matches the name beside it.

config_set.name: model is an alias for defaults.model
config_set.note: `set` echoes the key as spelled, not the canonical one.

config_set.name: a model that is not in the catalog
config_set.note: The active model is left alone.

config_set.name: defaults.stream parses the value as a bool
config_set.note: `value` comes back as a JSON boolean, not the string that was sent.

config_set.name: a value that is not a bool
autonomy.enabled echoes the canonical key
config_set.note: Unlike the model arm, this one reports `autonomy.enabled` whichever alias was sent.

config_set.name: a key that is not settable at runtime
config_set.note: The message lists the three that are.

err.message: Config key not settable at runtime: memory.mode. Supported: defaults.model, defaults.stream, autonomy.enabled

config_reload.name: check mode reports without applying
config_reload.note: No `prompts_refreshed` field at all in check mode — not `false`.

config_reload.name: a truthy non-boolean apply is not an apply
config_reload.note: `as_bool` on a number is `None`, so both flags fall back to false and this is check mode.

config_reload.name: apply adopts the config on disk
config_reload.note: `state_after` is the whole point: three chat models now, and `defaults_model` moved.

config_reload.name: a broken config aborts before adopting anything
config_reload.note: `state_after` still shows the original config — the failure is before any mutation.

config_reload.name: a broken character overlay aborts the reload
config_reload.note: The overlay is validated against the *fresh* global config, so a typo in one character's config.toml stops the whole reload rather than silently falling back at merge time.

invalid array
expected `]`

config_reload.name: check mode lists the prompt files that differ
config_reload.note: SOUL.md differs from its snapshot and USER.md matches, so exactly one file is reported. Nothing is applied.

config_reload.name: a prompt file with no snapshot at all is changed
apply with refresh_prompts activates the pending edits
config_reload.note: `prompts_refreshed` is true only on this path. `changed_after` is what says the snapshot was actually rewritten: the same call in check mode leaves it non-empty.

config_reload.name: apply without refresh_prompts leaves the snapshot alone
config_reload.note: The mirror of the case above: same tree, same adopt, but `changed_after` still lists SOUL.md.

config_reset.name: reset drops runtime overrides and reloads from disk
config_reset.note: `defaults_stream` goes back to the file's `false`, and `active_model` back to null.

config_reset.name: reset with a broken config on disk
config_reset.note: `internal_error` here, where `config_reload` reports `invalid_request` for the same file.
